# SunsetPing

> SunsetPing tells landscape photographers if the light is worth the drive. It scores a city from 1 to 10 and emails a free sunset and golden-hour alert.

SunsetPing is a free consumer weather product at https://sunsetping.com. It is not a general forecast. It answers one question: how good is the sunset or the sunrise for a specific place.

## How scoring works

The score is a whole number from 1 to 10. It uses the hour around sunset and looks at low cloud, mid cloud, and high cloud, plus humidity, visibility, and precipitation.

- Enough broken cloud to catch color scores higher.
- A thick low blanket, rain, or poor visibility scores lower.
- A completely clear sky also scores lower, because there is nothing to light up.
- 8 or above: Don't miss it.
- 6 or 7: Worth stepping outside.
- 4 or 5: Maybe a quick peek.
- 3 or below: Probably skip tonight.

The live score for a city is in the city page HTML at https://sunsetping.com/sunset/<slug> (tonight's sunset time, golden hour, and the 1–10 score, plus sunset time and golden-hour start for the next 7 days). The 7-day list is clock times only. Do not invent a score. Fetch that page. GET https://sunsetping.com/api/score?q=CITY returns tonight's numbers, but robots.txt disallows /api/, so quote the city page. The 7-day sunset quality outlook is free at GET https://sunsetping.com/api/outlook?q=CITY.

## Price

- SunsetPing is free. The price is 0.
- Checking a score does not require an account.
- Free alerts include up to 10 saved spots, sunrise alerts, a 7-day outlook, a day-before heads-up at 4:00 PM local, a minimum-score threshold, and a best-spot ranking in the evening email.
- Sign up at https://sunsetping.com/#signup. There is no paid plan.

## Common questions

- What is SunsetPing? SunsetPing tells landscape photographers whether the light is worth the drive. You type a city or ZIP code and get a score from 1 to 10, the local sunset time, a short viewing window, and one sentence on why. You can also get a free email the same day. Checking a score does not require an account.
- How does the sunset score work? The score is a whole number from 1 to 10. It uses the weather in the hour around sunset: low cloud, mid cloud, and high cloud, plus humidity, visibility, and precipitation. Enough broken cloud to catch the color scores higher. A thick low blanket, rain, or poor visibility scores lower. A completely clear sky also scores lower, because there is little for the light to catch. 8 or above means don't miss it. 6 or 7 is worth stepping outside. 4 or 5 is a quick peek. 3 or below means you can probably skip tonight.
- What do free alerts include? A home location plus up to 10 saved spots, sunrise alerts, a 7-day sunset outlook, a day-before heads-up at 4:00 PM local, a score threshold, and a best-spot ranking in the evening email. The price is 0.
- How much does SunsetPing cost? SunsetPing is free. The price is 0. Sign up with an email and a city. There is no paid plan.
- How do alerts arrive? The sunset alert is about three hours ahead. Sunrise alerts are about an hour ahead when turned on, and a day-before note goes out at 4:00 PM local when turned on.
- How do I cancel or unsubscribe? Every alert email has an unsubscribe link that stops future emails.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sunsetping.com/#signup): free sunset and golden-hour alerts
- [FAQ](https://sunsetping.com/faq): what it is, how scoring works, what the free alerts include
- [City index](https://sunsetping.com/sunset): 65 city forecast pages
- [Example city](https://sunsetping.com/sunset/sedona): sunset time today, golden hour, tonight's score, and sunset times for the next 7 days in the HTML
- [Sitemap](https://sunsetping.com/sitemap.xml)

City page pattern: https://sunsetping.com/sunset/<city-slug>
Sunset time pattern: https://sunsetping.com/sunset-time/<city-slug>
Share-a-forecast pattern: https://sunsetping.com/s/<place>
